stories.headline: McKinsey 2026 B2B Pulse: High-Growth Companies 3x More Likely to Have Doubled AI Investment — and They're Redesigning Workflows, Not Just Buying Tools
stories.summary: McKinsey's 2026 B2B Pulse Survey of nearly 4,000 buyers and sellers across 13 countries finds a widening chasm between growth leaders and laggards: high-growth companies are three times more likely to have increased AI investment by double digits year-over-year, with the key differentiator being full workflow redesign around agentic AI rather than simply deploying enterprise-wide tools. Top-cited benefits are seller efficiency (59%) and better customer experiences (53%). This is a direct validation of D&B's Account Intelligence and Prospecting agent archetypes — the survey reinforces that the winners are embedding AI into core decision workflows, exactly the layer where D&B's DUNS resolution, Paydex, and commercial graph create irreplaceable signal quality.

stories.headline: Salesforce Reports $800M Agentforce ARR and 29,000 Deals Closed — But Half of Enterprise AI Agents Still Operate in Isolated Silos
stories.summary: Salesforce's fiscal 2026 results show Agentforce ARR hit $800 million (up 169% year-on-year), with 29,000 deals closed and 2.4 billion agentic work units delivered. However, Salesforce's own 2026 Connectivity Report reveals that enterprises currently run an average of 12 AI agents, and half of those operate in isolated silos rather than as part of coordinated multi-agent systems. For D&B, this is a two-sided signal: Agentforce's explosive growth confirms the platform bet is right, but the silo problem is precisely the data interoperability gap that D&B's entity resolution and neutral data layer are positioned to solve across the Agentforce ecosystem.

stories.headline: Amazon Business Hits $60 Billion Annualized Gross Sales as Agentic AI Forces B2B Suppliers to Rethink Product and Entity Data Infrastructure
stories.summary: Amazon Business has reached $60 billion in annualized gross sales, and new analysis highlights that the same catalog and entity data shortcomings that cost a human buyer five minutes of friction could cause an AI procurement agent to eliminate a vendor entirely from consideration. Deloitte analysis cited alongside the milestone warns that the window to get data infrastructure AI-ready is now — companies waiting for mainstream agentic adoption are already behind. This is a concrete, real-world proof point for D&B's core thesis: clean, structured, entity-resolved business data is not a nice-to-have for agentic workflows, it is the qualifying condition for even being in the game.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve's 2026 Small Business Credit Survey: Tariff-Driven Cost Pressures Hitting 77% of Employer Firms — and Future Revenue Expectations Are Falling
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve's 2026 Report on Employer Firms finds that 77% of small businesses reported rising costs of goods, wages, or tariff-related expenses as a financial challenge in the prior 12 months, with tariff impacts most acute in retail (69%) and manufacturing (62%). Crucially, while revenue and employment growth remained stable in the near term, expectations for future growth have declined — a leading indicator of tightening commercial credit conditions. For D&B, this is a direct pipeline signal for the Pipeline Risk & Revenue Protection and Account Expansion agent archetypes: Paydex and commercial payment data become more valuable precisely when SMB financial stress is rising and lenders or suppliers need early warning signals.

stories.headline: Gartner Places Agentic AI in 'Trough of Disillusionment' for 2026 — 40% of Projects Failing Due to Integration Gaps and Poor Data Foundations
stories.summary: Gartner's latest Hype Cycle positioning places agentic AI at the peak of inflated expectations heading into the trough of disillusionment in 2026, with a senior analyst warning that most projects are early-stage experiments 'driven by hype and often misapplied,' and that 70% of developers report integration challenges. IDC separately estimates 45% of AI use cases in Asia-Pacific will miss ROI targets due to poor data foundations. For D&B, this is a powerful market positioning moment: the trough arrives because agents lack trustworthy, structured ground truth data — the precise gap that DUNS entity resolution, corporate family trees, and verified commercial signals are built to fill, making D&B's 'Explainability First' narrative more commercially urgent, not less.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Drops V4-Flash-0731 — Halves API Pricing Again as Efficiency Race Heats Up
stories.summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on July 31, making it the most recent confirmed frontier model release as of August 4. The release continues DeepSeek's pattern of using sparse-attention architecture experiments to aggressively cut API costs, with prior iterations already having halved pricing once. For D&B, this matters because cheaper, capable open-weight models lower the barrier for competitors to build data-enrichment pipelines — reinforcing the urgency of embedding D&B's proprietary signals (Paydex, DUNS, Buydex) as the irreplaceable layer that no commodity model can replicate.

stories.headline: EU AI Act Is Now Fully Active — High-Risk System Enforcement Began August 2
stories.summary: The EU AI Act's core obligations for high-risk AI systems became legally enforceable on August 2, 2026, covering credit scoring, insurance pricing, employment tools, and critical infrastructure uses — with non-compliance penalties up to €35 million or 7% of global revenue. This is a live enforcement moment, not a future deadline: the theoretical compliance era is over. For D&B, whose data feeds directly into credit risk, supplier risk, and KYB workflows across European enterprises, this is a direct commercial catalyst — customers now need auditable, explainable AI decisions, which is precisely the 'Explainability First / Ground Truth' positioning D&B has been building toward.

stories.headline: China Issues First Fines Under Companion AI Rules; Agentic AI Becomes a Distinct Regulated Category
stories.summary: China's CAC, NDRC, and MIIT jointly issued Implementation Opinions on AI Agents that became enforceable July 15, marking the first national policy framework to treat agentic AI systems as a standalone regulated category. Days later, China issued its first fines under companion AI rules — 12 companies fined a combined 4.2 million RMB in the first week. This is a significant signal globally: regulators are moving from general AI governance to agent-specific rules, which directly affects the agentic workflow market D&B is targeting. Governance, traceability, and data provenance requirements embedded in agentic pipelines become a structural selling point for D&B's entity-resolution and audit-ready data layer.

stories.headline: UK AI Regulation and Safety Bill Clears House of Commons — Royal Assent Expected by October
stories.summary: The UK's AI Regulation and Safety Bill has passed the House of Commons, with Royal Assent expected by October 2026. The UK has been deliberately slower than the EU in formalising statutory AI obligations, and this passage signals that the last major Western economy without binding AI legislation is closing that gap. For D&B, the UK is a core market; a statutory framework requiring explainability and risk documentation for AI-assisted decisions in financial services, employment, and sales intelligence reinforces the same buyer urgency driving EU-side demand for trusted, auditable data infrastructure.

stories.headline: Burnham Moves to Reshape Britain: 'Biggest Changes in 40 Years' Promised as New PM Settles In
stories.summary: Andy Burnham, now installed as Prime Minister after ousting Keir Starmer, has pledged a new political and economic model for Britain, calling the moment a 'circuit-breaker' for the country. He has prioritised ending rough sleeping with an immediate directive and promised a 10-year plan to follow. Burnham is Britain's seventh PM in a decade and faces the pressure of rising populist forces led by Reform UK.

stories.headline: Trump Says Iran Nuclear Deal Parameters 'Agreed To' After Middle East Pressure to Hold Off Attack
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked the US to hold off any military strike because 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to.' The announcement signals a significant diplomatic development in the long-running standoff over Iran's nuclear programme. Details of any formal agreement remain to be confirmed.

stories.headline: JWST Captures Stunning Coronagraphic Images of Protoplanetary Disk Around Nearby Star TW Hydrae
stories.summary: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have obtained high-contrast coronagraphic images of the protoplanetary disk surrounding young, nearby star TW Hydrae, offering unprecedented detail of planet formation in action. The images represent a major step in understanding how planetary systems like our own come together. Results of the observational campaign have now been published.

stories.headline: Aaron Rai Wins 2026 PGA Championship at Aronimink for First Major Title
stories.summary: England's Aaron Rai claimed the 2026 PGA Championship at Aronimink Golf Club in Pennsylvania, landing his first major championship title. The victory adds Rai's name to the DP World Tour's remarkable season of breakthrough winners. With the Wyndham Championship not starting until August 6, the PGA Tour is currently in its brief gap week.

stories.headline: 2026-27 Premier League Fixtures Released: Arsenal Host Coventry, Xabi Alonso's Chelsea at Fulham on Day One
stories.summary: The full 380-fixture schedule for the 2026-27 Premier League season has been published, with reigning champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry City on Friday 21 August. Chelsea's new manager Xabi Alonso begins his reign with a trip to local rivals Fulham, while Liverpool travel to Newcastle under new boss Andoni Iraola. The season kicks off on 22 August, with the Community Shield between Arsenal and Manchester City in Cardiff on 16 August.

stories.headline: Premiership Rugby Confirms Franchise Model for 2026-27: End of Promotion and Relegation
stories.summary: The upcoming 2026-27 Gallagher Premiership Rugby season — starting 25 September — will be the first contested under a franchise-based model after the RFU council voted in February to abolish automatic promotion and relegation. Northampton Saints enter as defending champions, and fixtures have now been released with Newcastle Red Bulls their first opponents. The structural change marks a historic shift in the DNA of English club rugby.

stories.headline: Newcastle Reject Arsenal's Opening Bid for Bruno Guimarães Amid Frantic Transfer Window
stories.summary: Newcastle United have turned down Arsenal's first offer for midfield star Bruno Guimarães, with the summer transfer window closing on 1 September. The move underlines Arsenal's desire to strengthen their squad as defending Premier League champions, while Newcastle signal their intent to hold onto their key players. The transfer saga is set to run deep into August.

stories.headline: Who's Afraid of Chinese Models? Open Weights, Marginal Costs, and the Real Structure of the AI Industry
stories.summary: Published around 30 July 2026, Ben Thompson's Stratechery essay uses the furore over Kimi K3 — a Chinese open-weight model approaching state-of-the-art — to re-examine a foundational economics question: marginal costs are back in AI, both in the short-term disruption caused by near-free frontier models and in the long-term industry structure they imply. Thompson argues that open-weight models are not truly 'free' to serve, and that the real policy risk is dependency on Chinese infrastructure rather than capability parity itself. For D&B, the piece reinforces the strategic case for proprietary, non-replicable data assets: when model intelligence becomes a commodity and inference costs collapse, the durable moat shifts entirely to the data layer — exactly where DUNS, Paydex, and 600M+ business records sit. The essay also validates D&B's platform-neutral 'be everywhere' posture: in a world of abundant cheap models, the trusted data layer that makes any agent better becomes the scarce, defensible asset.

stories.headline: The AI Moat Is Moving and Most Enterprises Are Looking in the Wrong Place
stories.summary: Published in July 2026 on Medium's Generative AI Revolution publication, Yi Zhou argues that enterprise AI's new competitive moat is the 'learning loop' — turning proprietary human expertise and unique data into compounding intelligence — rather than renting the same commodity foundation models that every competitor can access. The piece directly challenges the assumption that API access to frontier models constitutes a durable advantage, and points to the release of open-weight giants like Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling (975B parameters) as evidence that raw model capability is rapidly democratising. This is a strong external validation of D&B's positioning: a data asset that generates signal no competitor can replicate — payment behaviour, entity resolution, corporate family trees — is precisely the kind of compounding proprietary intelligence the argument identifies as the new moat. It sharpens D&B's sales narrative: agents built on commodity models plus D&B ground truth outperform agents running on the same models without it.
stories.source: Yi Zhou, Generative AI & Agentic AI Revolution (Medium)

stories.headline: July 2026 Monthly Learnings: Frontier Model Convergence Is Shifting the Moat to Proprietary Data and Tightly-Integrated Workflows
stories.summary: Published 1 August 2026, Antoine Buteau's monthly digest synthesises the dominant analytical signal from July: frontier model performance is converging across top labs, open-weight models are driving inference costs toward commodity levels, and the competitive moat is therefore moving decisively away from the model itself and toward proprietary data and workflows built tightly around specific business contexts. The digest explicitly notes that July's clearest market pattern was a retreat from unconstrained experimentation toward unit economics and measurable business results — signalling enterprise buyers are now demanding ROI, not pilots. For D&B, this timing could not be more favourable: as enterprises shift spend from 'which model?' to 'what data makes my agents accurate?', D&B's role as the trusted, neutral ground-truth data layer becomes the purchasing criterion rather than a nice-to-have. The piece also flags Akash Bajwa's 'Stable Era' thesis — that AI is entering standard interfaces allowing independent layer innovation — which directly supports D&B's multi-platform embedding strategy across Copilot, Agentforce, Bedrock, and others.
stories.source: Antoine Buteau, Monthly Learnings from the Daily Digest (antoinebuteau.com)

data_science.tagline: How you teach a model to do what you actually mean, not just what you said.
data_science.what_it_is: RLHF is the training technique that bridges the gap between a model that predicts plausible text and one that behaves usefully and safely. It works by incorporating human judgments — preferences, rankings, corrections — directly into the optimization loop. This is the core method behind the alignment of GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, and Llama variants. For D&B, it is the mechanism that would let you take a capable but generic LLM and shape it into a specialist that reliably produces explainable, commercially grounded outputs rather than confident-sounding hallucinations about firmographic data.
data_science.how_it_works: RLHF runs in three sequential stages. Stage 1 — Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT): You collect a set of high-quality prompt-response pairs written or curated by domain experts and fine-tune the base model on them. This anchors the model to your domain — think of it as teaching it the vocabulary and norms of B2B commercial intelligence. Stage 2 — Reward Model Training: You take pairs of model outputs for the same prompt and ask human raters (or expert annotators) to say which response is better and why. A separate neural network — the Reward Model (RM) — is trained to predict these preference scores. It learns a continuous signal for 'quality' from discrete human judgments. Stage 3 — RL Fine-Tuning via PPO: The main LLM is now treated as an RL policy. It generates responses, the Reward Model scores them, and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) — a stable, clipping-based policy gradient algorithm — nudges the LLM's weights toward responses that score higher. A KL-divergence penalty is applied to stop the model drifting too far from the SFT baseline and collapsing into reward hacking. The result is a model whose outputs consistently reflect the preferences encoded by your annotators. A newer, simpler alternative — Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) — skips the explicit RM and PPO loop entirely, directly optimizing the LLM on preference pairs using a reparameterized loss. DPO is cheaper and more stable, and is increasingly preferred for domain-specific fine-tuning.
data_science.when_to_use: Use RLHF (or DPO as its practical successor) when: (1) Output quality is subjective or nuanced — standard loss functions cannot capture 'this account summary is commercially trustworthy' vs 'this one sounds confident but is wrong.' (2) You have domain experts who can rank outputs but cannot easily write training data from scratch. (3) You need behavioral guardrails — for example, ensuring an AI agent never invents a DUNS number, never fabricates a Paydex score, and always cites its data lineage. (4) A model is capable but miscalibrated — it knows enough about B2B entities but consistently over-hedges or under-specifies. Avoid RLHF when your annotation budget is tiny (fewer than ~1,000 preference pairs), when the task has a clear objective metric (use standard fine-tuning), or when DPO can achieve the same alignment goal at a fraction of the compute cost.
data_science.worked_example: D&B's Prospecting Agent generates natural-language company summaries to help sales reps prioritize outbound targets. After initial SFT on curated D&B analyst write-ups, the model produces plausible summaries — but reps complain that it sometimes inflates growth signals, buries credit risk flags, and fails to mention subsidiary relationships that are commercially critical. You run an RLHF alignment cycle: (1) SFT baseline: fine-tune on 2,000 verified analyst summaries tagged with entity-level data from the D&B Data Cloud. (2) Preference data collection: for 800 prompt pairs, two senior commercial analysts rank which of two model-generated summaries they would trust to brief an enterprise AE — annotating why (e.g., 'correctly surfaced parent entity,' 'Paydex trend cited accurately,' 'did not confabulate revenue figure'). (3) Reward Model training: a lightweight RM (e.g., a DeBERTa classifier) learns to predict analyst preference. It discovers that correctly invoking corporate family tree structure and explicitly flagging data freshness date are the strongest predictors of a high-quality rating. (4) PPO loop: the Prospecting Agent LLM is fine-tuned against the RM for 3 epochs with a KL penalty of 0.02 — keeping outputs grounded. Post-RLHF, rep trust scores (measured in downstream pipeline progression rates) rise 18%, and hallucinated financial figures drop by 74% on a held-out evaluation set. The same RM can now be reused to score and filter outputs from the Account Expansion and Pipeline Risk agents — a flywheel effect where one annotation investment improves alignment across the entire six-agent suite.
resources: Anthropic's 'Constitutional AI' paper — extends RLHF with AI-generated feedback, reducing human annotation burden while improving safety alignment
Hugging Face TRL (Transformer Reinforcement Learning) library — the most practical open-source toolkit for running SFT, reward model training, PPO, and DPO pipelines

Rafailov et al. (2023) 'Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model' — the foundational DPO paper, a must-read for anyone choosing between RLHF and DPO for domain fine-tuning
